Proper storage is crucial to keep your eggs fresh for a longer period.
Here are some tips to help you store your eggs:
**Cool, dry place:** Store eggs in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat sources.
**Refrigerate:** Store eggs in the refrigerator at a consistent temperature below 40°F (4°C).
This will help prevent bacterial growth and keep eggs fresh for a longer period.
**Carton or container:** Store eggs in their original carton or a covered container to protect them from moisture, light, and contamination.
Make sure the container is clean and dry before placing the eggs inside.
**Pointed end down:** Store eggs with the pointed end down to prevent the yolk from coming into contact with the shell membrane, which can cause bacterial contamination.
**Don't wash:** Avoid washing eggs before storing them.
Washing can remove the natural coating on the eggshell, making it more susceptible to bacterial penetration.
**Check regularly:** Regularly check your eggs for cracks, breaks, or unusual odors.
Remove any spoiled eggs to prevent contamination.
**First-in, first-out:** Use the oldest eggs first to ensure you're consuming the freshest eggs.
**Label and date:** Label the carton or container with the date you collected the eggs, so you can keep track of their age.
**Don't stack:** Avoid stacking eggs on top of each other, as this can cause pressure and lead to breakage.
**Freezing:** If you have an excess of eggs, you can freeze them.
